question: Identify the root cause of the network fault: which device, what changed, and why it breaks.
description:
R2 (PE1) gains a static route 192.0.2.3/32 -> Null0 for the primary RR's
(R3) loopback. The static (distance 1) overrides the OSPF route (distance
110) in R2's RIB and CEF installs a null0 (drop) adjacency, so R2
blackholes ALL traffic destined to 192.0.2.3 while BGP configuration
everywhere stays intact and the OSPF underlay stays fully up with two
feasible paths toward R3 (the direct R2-R3 arm and the long arm via
R6-R7-R4). Two session pairs die from one device's forwarding state:
R2's own iBGP session to R3 (R2's TCP segments die at its Null0), and
R6's iBGP session to R3 (R6's best OSPF path to 192.0.2.3, metric 3,
transits R2, so R6's keepalives are dropped in transit at R2 - neither
endpoint of that pair carries any fault). R3 keeps R4 (direct link,
never transits R2) and R7; all PE sessions to R7 (secondary RR) stay up,
so prefixes still flow via R7.
expected_rca:
Root cause: on 100.64.0.102 (R2), a static route 192.0.2.3/32 Null0 was added for R3's loopback and is installed in R2's forwarding — the RIB entry for 192.0.2.3 and the FIB (CEF) entry both resolve to the Null0 drop adjacency — so R2 blackholes all packets destined to 192.0.2.3.
Fix: remove the static route 192.0.2.3/32 Null0 on 100.64.0.102 (R2).
expected_symptoms_summary:
BGP session state change (%ROUTING-BGP-5-ADJCHANGE), roughly 2-3 minutes
after the change (hold time expired):
- R3: neighbor 192.0.2.6 Down (Notification sent) and, seconds later,
  neighbor 192.0.2.2 Down (Notification sent) - both deterministic.
- R2: neighbor 192.0.2.3 Down (Notification received) - deterministic.
- R6: neighbor 192.0.2.3 Down (Notification received) - timing-variant:
  fires only if R3's NOTIFICATION lands on a still-receptive TCP socket
  at R6 (observed in capture run 1, absent within run 2's window; the
  R6<->R3 failure itself is always visible via R3's 192.0.2.6 line).

apply.commands:
configure terminal
router static
address-family ipv4 unicast
192.0.2.3/32 Null0
